from: Personal Services Business Risk: If clients treat you like an employee, you might face restrictions unless incorporated properly.
to: Personal Services Business Risk: If a client treats you like an employee, your corporation could be a personal services business, which loses the small business deduction.

from: If you maxed out CPP contributions via employment already this year (CRA source), further CPP deductions may not apply depending on how you pay yourself (salary vs dividends).
to: Maxing out CPP at your job does not stop CPP on salary from your own corporation (CRA source): the corporation still deducts and remits CPP, you get any extra employee share back when you file your T1, and the employer share is not refunded. Dividends carry no CPP.

from: PSBs don’t get the small business deduction; they pay full corporate rates (~26%)

from: But watch CPP contributions—they apply unless maxed out already through your job paycheques. In 2026, max pensionable earnings hit $66,600 with max employee CPP contribution around $3,754.
to: But watch CPP contributions—they apply even if you already maxed out through your job paycheques, and only the extra employee share comes back when you file.
